lesson.menu_title: What I Meant Was -- Reported Speech for Summarizing Client Calls, Legal Advice and Meeting Outcomes at ALMA
lesson.menu_desc: Turning a forty-minute client call into five lines a partner can act on: tense backshift, reported questions and requests, and the reporting verb that carries the risk -- 35 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 9 -- Reporting the Room
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Leonardo Constantino | Lesson 9 -- Reported Speech
lesson.grammar_point: reported speech (backshift, reported questions and requests, reporting verbs)

listenings.text: Leonardo, this is the general counsel at Meridian, calling before our meeting so that you are not hearing any of this for the first time on the call. Three things. The board approved the amendment on the second of October, and I can send you the minutes, but nothing has been filed yet, and I would rather you heard that from me. Second, we have received no notification from the authority. Nothing. I went through the whole file this morning and there is no acknowledgment anywhere in the correspondence, which after four months is starting to worry me more than the amendment does. Third, and this is the reason I am calling, our tax director will ask you about the disclosure, and he will ask you in front of the chief financial officer. If your answer is that it does not cover the Mexican entity, say so directly. Do not soften it. Before Thursday, please confirm the filing date in writing, and send me one page. One. The last note your team sent ran to eleven, and nobody in that room read past the second.

I want to tell you about a single word that cost a client four months. An associate on my team wrote a meeting note after a call, and in it he wrote that the client had said the position was safe. That is what he heard. But the client had not said it was safe. The client had warned us that it was not, and had asked twice whether we thought the authority would accept it. The associate used the wrong verb, and for four months everybody who opened that file read the word said and moved on, because said sounds neutral and neutral things do not need action. Here is the thing nobody teaches you at law school. A meeting note is not a transcript. Nobody wants every word in the order it was spoken. What a note records is who committed to what, and how strongly. So choose the verb before you write the sentence. If somebody flagged a risk, they warned. If somebody made it certain, they confirmed. If somebody only gave a signal, they indicated, and you must not upgrade that to confirmed because it reads better. The verb is the part somebody will rely on a year from now, in a room you are not in.

extra_audio.text: The general counsel confirmed that the board had approved the amendment. She warned that no notification had arrived from the authority. Their tax director asked whether the disclosure covered the Mexican entity. We advised that the disclosure should be amended before the deadline. The client gave an undertaking to confirm the filing date in writing.
